result:
I found one real bug in `dparse.parser`: a regex denial of service (ReDoS) when parsing index-server lines. It's the known CVE-2022-39280, and I wrote it up in `bug_report_dparse_parser_2026-10-06_06-48_0b8l.md`.

**The bug (High severity):** any `-i`, `--index-url` or `--extra-index-url` line in a requirements file goes to `Parser.parse_index_server`, which searches it with `URL_REGEX.findall`. That regex has overlapping repeated parts, and `findall` retries from every position. A line made of a URL scheme repeated many times therefore makes parsing time grow with the cube of the line length:

| Line length | Parse time |
|---|---|
| 1.6 KB (`"https://" * 200`) | 0.11 s |
| 3.2 KB | 0.85 s |
| 6.4 KB | 6.66 s |

A file of about 13 KB would stall for roughly a minute (extrapolated, not run). dparse is meant to read dependency files from untrusted repos, for example in vulnerability scanners, so one crafted file can hang whatever uses it.

Hypothesis found this independently. The shrunk failing input was `"--index-url " + "http://11:" * 398`, a single 4 KB line. My first version of the test passed only because random text almost never contains `https://`; it failed once the generated text was made to start with a URL scheme.

**Proposed fix (in the report):** take the token right after the option name by splitting on `=` or whitespace, instead of searching with the regex. I checked it by patching it in: the existing `test_index_server` and `test_requirements_package_with_index_server` tests still pass, and a 40 KB line parses in under 1 ms. I didn't edit the library itself.

**Other properties tested, all passing:**
- A well-formed index URL comes back unchanged, with a trailing `/` added if missing.
- That index server gets attached to the dependencies listed after it.
- `--hash=` values are extracted in order.
- Arbitrary text in a requirements file doesn't crash the parser.

Everything is in `runs/dparse_r5/`: the tests are in `test_dparse_parser.py`, the reproduction script is `repro.py`, and the fix check is `check_fix.py`.

Separately, several claude.ai connectors (Asana, Atlassian, Box, Canva, Figma, HubSpot, Intercom, Linear, Notion, monday.com) need to be authorized in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This task didn't need them.
